knowledge_point.title: Calculating the Gradient of a Function of Two Variables

question.:question/problem: Evaluate $\nabla f(x,y)$ at $(1,2)$ if $f(x,y)=e^{- x y - y^{2} + 7}$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Differentiate with respect to one coordinate at a time, holding the other constant.

$$
\begin{aligned}f_x(x,y)&=- ye^{- y^{2} - y x + 7} \\ &=- y e^{- x y - y^{2} + 7} \\ f_y(x,y)&=(- 2 y - x)e^{- y^{2} - y x + 7} \\ &=\left(- x - 2 y\right) e^{- x y - y^{2} + 7}\end{aligned}
$$

Assemble the partial derivatives in order:

$$
\begin{aligned}\nabla f(x,y)&=(- y e^{- x y - y^{2} + 7})\,\mathbf i \\ &\quad+(\left(- x - 2 y\right) e^{- x y - y^{2} + 7})\,\mathbf j\end{aligned}
$$

Now substitute the point:

$$
\begin{aligned}f_x(1,2)&=- \left(2\right) e^{- \left(1\right) \left(2\right) - \left(2\right)^{2} + 7} \\ &=- 2 e \\ f_y(1,2)&=\left(- \left(1\right) - 2 \left(2\right)\right) e^{- \left(1\right) \left(2\right) - \left(2\right)^{2} + 7} \\ &=- 5 e\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $\nabla f(1,2)=\langle - 2 e,\,- 5 e\rangle$.

question.:question/problem: Find $\nabla f(x,y)$ if $f(x,y)=\frac{2 x - 3 y}{- x + y}$. Work on the domain $y - x\ne0$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Apply the quotient rule to each partial. The denominator-derivative contribution is subtracted in both components.

$$
\begin{aligned}f_x(x,y)&=\frac{(2)(y - x)-(- 3 y + 2 x)(-1)}{(y - x)^2} \\ &=- \frac{y}{\left(- x + y\right)^{2}} \\ f_y(x,y)&=\frac{(-3)(y - x)-(- 3 y + 2 x)\cdot1}{(y - x)^2} \\ &=\frac{x}{\left(- x + y\right)^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Assemble the partial derivatives in order:

$$
\begin{aligned}\nabla f(x,y)&=\left(- \frac{y}{\left(- x + y\right)^{2}}\right)\,\mathbf i \\ &\quad+\left(\frac{x}{\left(- x + y\right)^{2}}\right)\,\mathbf j.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Find $\nabla f(x,y)$ if $f(x,y)=- 3 \ln{\left(x y \right)} + 2 \cos{\left(x^{2} \right)}$. Work on the domain $yx>0$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Differentiate with respect to one coordinate at a time, holding the other constant.

$$
\begin{aligned}f_x(x,y)&=\frac{-3}{yx}\cdot y-2\sin(x^{2})\cdot 2 x \\ &=- 4 x \sin{\left(x^{2} \right)} - \frac{3}{x} \\ f_y(x,y)&=\frac{-3}{yx}\cdot x+0 \\ &=- \frac{3}{y}\end{aligned}
$$

Assemble the partial derivatives in order:

$$
\begin{aligned}\nabla f(x,y)&=(- 4 x \sin{\left(x^{2} \right)} - \frac{3}{x})\,\mathbf i \\ &\quad+\left(- \frac{3}{y}\right)\,\mathbf j.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Evaluate $\nabla f(x,y)$ at $(2,1)$ if $f(x,y)=- 3 x^{2} + 2 x y + 2 x - 3 y^{2}$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Differentiate with respect to one coordinate at a time, holding the other constant.

$$
\begin{aligned}f_x(x,y)&=0+2 y- 6 x+2 \\ &=- 6 x + 2 y + 2 \\ f_y(x,y)&=- 6 y+2 x+0+0 \\ &=2 x - 6 y\end{aligned}
$$

Assemble the partial derivatives in order:

$$
\begin{aligned}\nabla f(x,y)&=(- 6 x + 2 y + 2)\,\mathbf i \\ &\quad+(2 x - 6 y)\,\mathbf j\end{aligned}
$$

Now substitute the point:

$$
\begin{aligned}f_x(2,1)&=- 6 \left(2\right) + 2 \left(1\right) + 2 \\ &=-8 \\ f_y(2,1)&=2 \left(2\right) - 6 \left(1\right) \\ &=-2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $\nabla f(2,1)=\langle -8,\,-2\rangle$.

question.:question/problem: Evaluate $\nabla f(x,y)$ at $(-2,3)$ if $f(x,y)=- y^{2} \sqrt{x + 11}$. Work on the domain $x + 11>0$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Differentiate with respect to one coordinate at a time, holding the other constant.

$$
\begin{aligned}f_x(x,y)&=- y^{2}\cdot\frac{1}{2\sqrt{x + 11}} \\ &=- \frac{y^{2}}{2 \sqrt{x + 11}} \\ f_y(x,y)&=- 2 y\sqrt{x + 11} \\ &=- 2 y \sqrt{x + 11}\end{aligned}
$$

Assemble the partial derivatives in order:

$$
\begin{aligned}\nabla f(x,y)&=\left(- \frac{y^{2}}{2 \sqrt{x + 11}}\right)\,\mathbf i \\ &\quad+(- 2 y \sqrt{x + 11})\,\mathbf j\end{aligned}
$$

Now substitute the point:

$$
\begin{aligned}f_x(-2,3)&=- \frac{\left(3\right)^{2}}{2 \sqrt{\left(-2\right) + 11}} \\ &=- \frac{3}{2} \\ f_y(-2,3)&=- 2 \left(3\right) \sqrt{\left(-2\right) + 11} \\ &=-18\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $\nabla f(-2,3)=\langle - \frac{3}{2},\,-18\rangle$.

question.:question/problem: Find $\nabla f(x,y)$ if $f(x,y)=2 y^{2} \ln{\left(x \right)} - 3 \sin{\left(x y \right)}$. Work on the domain $x>0$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Differentiate with respect to one coordinate at a time, holding the other constant.

$$
\begin{aligned}f_x(x,y)&=- 3 y \cos{\left(y x \right)}+2 y^{2}\cdot\frac{1}{x} \\ &=- 3 y \cos{\left(x y \right)} + \frac{2 y^{2}}{x} \\ f_y(x,y)&=- 3 x \cos{\left(y x \right)}+4 y \ln{\left(x \right)} \\ &=- 3 x \cos{\left(x y \right)} + 4 y \ln{\left(x \right)}\end{aligned}
$$

Assemble the partial derivatives in order:

$$
\begin{aligned}\nabla f(x,y)&=(- 3 y \cos{\left(x y \right)} + \frac{2 y^{2}}{x})\,\mathbf i \\ &\quad+(- 3 x \cos{\left(x y \right)} + 4 y \ln{\left(x \right)})\,\mathbf j.\end{aligned}
$$

:answer-field/choices.:answer/value: \langle - 3 y \cos{\left(x y \right)} + \frac{2 y^{2}}{x},\,- 3 x \cos{\left(x y \right)} + 4 y \ln{\left(x \right)}\rangle
\langle - 3 x \cos{\left(x y \right)} + \frac{2 y^{2}}{x},\,4 y \ln{\left(x \right)} - 3 y \cos{\left(x y \right)}\rangle
\langle - 3 y \cos{\left(x y \right)} + \frac{4 y^{2}}{x},\,- 3 x \cos{\left(x y \right)} + 2 y \ln{\left(x \right)}\rangle

question.:question/problem: Find $\nabla f(x,y)$ if $f(x,y)=\frac{2 x^{2} - 3 x y^{2}}{- 2 x + y}$. Work on the domain $y - 2 x\ne0$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Apply the quotient rule to each partial. The denominator-derivative contribution is subtracted in both components.

$$
\begin{aligned}f_x(x,y)&=\frac{(- 3 y^{2} + 4 x)(y - 2 x)-(- 3 y^{2} x + 2 x^{2})(-2)}{(y - 2 x)^2} \\ &=- \frac{4 x^{2} - 4 x y + 3 y^{3}}{\left(- 2 x + y\right)^{2}} \\ f_y(x,y)&=\frac{(- 6 y x)(y - 2 x)-(- 3 y^{2} x + 2 x^{2})\cdot1}{(y - 2 x)^2} \\ &=- \frac{x \left(- 12 x y + 2 x + 3 y^{2}\right)}{\left(- 2 x + y\right)^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Assemble the partial derivatives in order:

$$
\begin{aligned}\nabla f(x,y)&=\left(- \frac{4 x^{2} - 4 x y + 3 y^{3}}{\left(- 2 x + y\right)^{2}}\right)\,\mathbf i \\ &\quad+\left(- \frac{x \left(- 12 x y + 2 x + 3 y^{2}\right)}{\left(- 2 x + y\right)^{2}}\right)\,\mathbf j.\end{aligned}
$$

:answer-field/choices.:answer/value: \langle - \frac{4 x^{2} - 4 x y + 3 y^{3}}{\left(2 x - y\right)^{2}},\,\frac{x \left(12 x y - 2 x - 3 y^{2}\right)}{\left(2 x - y\right)^{2}}\rangle
\langle - \frac{12 x^{2} - 12 x y^{2} - 4 x y + 3 y^{3}}{\left(2 x - y\right)^{2}},\,\frac{x \left(12 x y + 2 x - 9 y^{2}\right)}{\left(2 x - y\right)^{2}}\rangle
\langle - \frac{10 x^{2} - 9 x y^{2} - 4 x y + 3 y^{3}}{\left(2 x - y\right)^{2}},\,\frac{x \left(12 x y - 2 x - 3 y^{2}\right)}{\left(2 x - y\right)^{2}}\rangle
\langle \frac{x \left(12 x y - 2 x - 3 y^{2}\right)}{\left(2 x - y\right)^{2}},\,- \frac{4 x^{2} - 4 x y + 3 y^{3}}{\left(2 x - y\right)^{2}}\rangle
\langle - \frac{12 x^{2} - 12 x y^{2} - 4 x y + 3 y^{3}}{\left(2 x - y\right)^{2}},\,\frac{x \left(12 x y - 2 x - 3 y^{2}\right)}{\left(2 x - y\right)^{2}}\rangle

question.:question/worked-solution:
Differentiate with respect to one coordinate at a time, holding the other constant.

$$
\begin{aligned}f_x(x,y)&=- 4 y\cdot\frac{1}{1+x^2} \\ &=- \frac{4 y}{x^{2} + 1} \\ f_y(x,y)&=-4\arctan(x) \\ &=- 4 \arctan{\left(x \right)}\end{aligned}
$$

Assemble the partial derivatives in order:

$$
\begin{aligned}\nabla f(x,y)&=\left(- \frac{4 y}{x^{2} + 1}\right)\,\mathbf i \\ &\quad+(- 4 \arctan{\left(x \right)})\,\mathbf j\end{aligned}
$$

Now substitute the point:

$$
\begin{aligned}f_x(-1,2)&=- \frac{4 \left(2\right)}{\left(-1\right)^{2} + 1} \\ &=-4 \\ f_y(-1,2)&=- 4 \arctan{\left(\left(-1\right) \right)} \\ &=\pi\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $\nabla f(-1,2)=\langle -4,\,\pi\rangle$.

question.:question/problem: Find $\nabla f(x,y)$ if $f(x,y)=- \arctan{\left(\frac{x}{3 y} \right)}$. Work on the domain $y\ne0$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Differentiate with respect to one coordinate at a time, holding the other constant.

$$
\begin{aligned}f_x(x,y)&=\frac{1}{1+\left(- \frac{x}{3 y}\right)^2}\cdot\frac{1}{- 3 y} \\ &=- \frac{3 y}{x^{2} + 9 y^{2}} \\ f_y(x,y)&=\frac{1}{1+\left(- \frac{x}{3 y}\right)^2}\cdot\left(-\frac{x}{- 3 y^{2}}\right) \\ &=\frac{3 x}{x^{2} + 9 y^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Assemble the partial derivatives in order:

$$
\begin{aligned}\nabla f(x,y)&=\left(- \frac{3 y}{x^{2} + 9 y^{2}}\right)\,\mathbf i \\ &\quad+\left(\frac{3 x}{x^{2} + 9 y^{2}}\right)\,\mathbf j.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Evaluate $\nabla f(x,y)$ at $(2,2)$ if $f(x,y)=y \ln{\left(- x + y + 2 \right)}$. Work on the domain $y - x + 2>0$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
For the second partial use the product and chain rules. For the first, the second factor is constant.

$$
\begin{aligned}f_x(x,y)&=y\cdot\frac{1}{y - x + 2}\cdot -1 \\ &=- \frac{y}{- x + y + 2} \\ f_y(x,y)&=1\cdot\ln(y - x + 2)+y\cdot\frac{1}{y - x + 2}\cdot 1 \\ &=\frac{y}{- x + y + 2} + \ln{\left(- x + y + 2 \right)}\end{aligned}
$$

Assemble the partial derivatives in order:

$$
\begin{aligned}\nabla f(x,y)&=\left(- \frac{y}{- x + y + 2}\right)\,\mathbf i \\ &\quad+(\frac{y}{- x + y + 2} + \ln{\left(- x + y + 2 \right)})\,\mathbf j\end{aligned}
$$

Now substitute the point:

$$
\begin{aligned}f_x(2,2)&=- \frac{\left(2\right)}{- \left(2\right) + \left(2\right) + 2} \\ &=-1 \\ f_y(2,2)&=\frac{\left(2\right)}{- \left(2\right) + \left(2\right) + 2} + \ln{\left(- \left(2\right) + \left(2\right) + 2 \right)} \\ &=\ln{\left(2 \right)} + 1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $\nabla f(2,2)=\langle -1,\,\ln{\left(2 \right)} + 1\rangle$.

question.:question/problem: Evaluate $\nabla f(x,y)$ at $(1,e^{2})$ if $f(x,y)=\left(- x + y\right) \left(x^{2} + \ln{\left(y \right)}\right)$. Work on the domain $y>0$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Both factors depend on each coordinate. Apply the product rule separately, holding the other coordinate constant.

$$
\begin{aligned}f_x(x,y)&=-1(x^{2} + \ln{\left(y \right)})+(y - x)(2 x) \\ &=- x^{2} + 2 x \left(- x + y\right) - \ln{\left(y \right)} \\ f_y(x,y)&=x^{2} + \ln{\left(y \right)}+(y - x)\cdot\frac{1}{y} \\ &=x^{2} + \ln{\left(y \right)} + \frac{- x + y}{y}\end{aligned}
$$

Assemble the partial derivatives in order:

$$
\begin{aligned}\nabla f(x,y)&=(- x^{2} + 2 x \left(- x + y\right) - \ln{\left(y \right)})\,\mathbf i \\ &\quad+(x^{2} + \ln{\left(y \right)} + \frac{- x + y}{y})\,\mathbf j\end{aligned}
$$

Now substitute the point:

$$
\begin{aligned}f_x(1,e^{2})&=- \left(1\right)^{2} + 2 \left(1\right) \left(- \left(1\right) + \left(e^{2}\right)\right) - \ln{\left(\left(e^{2}\right) \right)} \\ &=-5 + 2 e^{2} \\ f_y(1,e^{2})&=\left(1\right)^{2} + \ln{\left(\left(e^{2}\right) \right)} + \frac{- \left(1\right) + \left(e^{2}\right)}{\left(e^{2}\right)} \\ &=4 - e^{-2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $\nabla f(1,e^{2})=\langle -5 + 2 e^{2},\,4 - e^{-2}\rangle$.

question.:question/problem: Evaluate $\nabla f(x,y)$ at $(0,2)$ if $f(x,y)=- \ln{\left(x^{2} + y^{2} \right)}$. Work on the domain $y^2+x^2>0$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Differentiate with respect to one coordinate at a time, holding the other constant.

$$
\begin{aligned}f_x(x,y)&=\frac{-1}{y^2+x^2}\cdot 2x \\ &=- \frac{2 x}{x^{2} + y^{2}} \\ f_y(x,y)&=\frac{-1}{y^2+x^2}\cdot 2y \\ &=- \frac{2 y}{x^{2} + y^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Assemble the partial derivatives in order:

$$
\begin{aligned}\nabla f(x,y)&=\left(- \frac{2 x}{x^{2} + y^{2}}\right)\,\mathbf i \\ &\quad+\left(- \frac{2 y}{x^{2} + y^{2}}\right)\,\mathbf j\end{aligned}
$$

Now substitute the point:

$$
\begin{aligned}f_x(0,2)&=- \frac{2 \left(0\right)}{\left(0\right)^{2} + \left(2\right)^{2}} \\ &=0 \\ f_y(0,2)&=- \frac{2 \left(2\right)}{\left(0\right)^{2} + \left(2\right)^{2}} \\ &=-1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $\nabla f(0,2)=\langle 0,\,-1\rangle$.

question.:question/worked-solution:
Use the product rule in each coordinate, including the chain derivative of the exponential.

$$

Assemble the partial derivatives in order:

$$
\begin{aligned}\nabla f(x,y)&=(\left(\frac{1}{y} + \frac{2}{x}\right) e^{- \frac{2 y}{x}})\,\mathbf i \\ &\quad+(\left(- \frac{x}{y^{2}} - \frac{2}{y}\right) e^{- \frac{2 y}{x}})\,\mathbf j.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Evaluate $\nabla f(x,y)$ at $(2,e)$ if $f(x,y)=y^{- 2 x}$. Work on the domain $y>0$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
In the second partial, the exponent is constant. In the first, the positive base is constant, so use exponential differentiation and the chain rule.

$$
\begin{aligned}f_x(x,y)&=y^{- 2 x}\ln(y)\cdot -2 \\ &=- 2 y^{- 2 x} \ln{\left(y \right)} \\ f_y(x,y)&=- 2 x\cdot y^{- 2 x - 1} \\ &=- 2 x y^{- 2 x - 1}\end{aligned}
$$

Assemble the partial derivatives in order:

$$
\begin{aligned}\nabla f(x,y)&=(- 2 y^{- 2 x} \ln{\left(y \right)})\,\mathbf i \\ &\quad+(- 2 x y^{- 2 x - 1})\,\mathbf j\end{aligned}
$$

Now substitute the point:

$$
\begin{aligned}f_x(2,e)&=- 2 \left(e\right)^{- 2 \left(2\right)} \ln{\left(\left(e\right) \right)} \\ &=- \frac{2}{e^{4}} \\ f_y(2,e)&=- 2 \left(2\right) \left(e\right)^{- 2 \left(2\right) - 1} \\ &=- \frac{4}{e^{5}}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $\nabla f(2,e)=\langle - \frac{2}{e^{4}},\,- \frac{4}{e^{5}}\rangle$.
